title: A joint AST–ALT surface does not establish incremental grip-strength prediction beyond enzyme levels and the De Ritis ratio across two NHANES cohorts
abstract: We tested whether joint AST–ALT spline interactions improve concurrent combined-handgrip prediction beyond additive enzyme levels, the De Ritis ratio, and conventional covariates. Models fitted in NHANES2011–2012 (n=4008) were frozen before evaluation in separately recruited2013–2014 participants (n=4531). Adding25 centered tensor-product terms changed examination-weighted mean squared error by +0.05274 kg² (joint source/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.26053,+9.20289]). The registered improvement criterion failed. This reused-data negative prediction audit does not establish physiological absence, equivalence, or external clinical utility. Independent-program validation remains incomplete.
